headline: Approved emergency RTU-1 repairs, deep cleaning, tree trimming, and a $2,195-a-month janitorial contract, among other spending.
summary: Staff reported on building repairs, mold retesting, and a tentative reopening date that depends on the retest results. Members also accepted donations from the Friends of the Leach Library and an anonymous donor, and delayed a vote on the library director job posting.

plain_text:
Leach Library Board of Trustees
Draft Meeting minutes
August 10, 2026 at 7:00 PM
Moose Hill Council Chambers, Town Hall, Londonderry NH
Members Present:
 Nancy Hendricks, Chair
 Beth Marrocco, Vice-Chair
 Azra Palo, Treasurer
 Erica Laue, Secretary
 Maryam Mallick, Trustee
 Donna Plante, Interim Library Director
Members Absent:
 Jan McLaughlin, Trustee
 Moira Ryan, Trustee
Call to Order: made at 7:01 PM by Chair Hendricks
Consent Agenda:
 Approval of minutes from July 22, 2026
 Next meetings: August 20 and September 3
 Motion to approve the consent agenda made by Secretary Laue, seconded by Vice
Chair Marrocco. Interim Director Plante recommended revising the July 22 minutes to 
reflect the reasons for the unanticipated fund donations. Motion revised by Secretary 
Laue to reflect those changes, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 
5-0.
Public Comment: None
Staff Reports: presented by Interim Director Plante
 The building project is on track. Carpeting is under installation and is looking good, and 
roof testing is underway. The entryway leak reappeared after the heavy rain last week, 
and the theory remains that Rooftop Unit 1 is the cause.
o RTU-1 was also identified as a point of failure during last week’s higher-than-
average temperatures. It was given a temporary fix, but it will need a 
replacement. Tonight’s vote has an item for a condensate pan for RTU-1 as a 
result.
 One of the brand-new ceiling tiles showed stains from leakage, and the valve above it 
was found to be failing. It was replaced.
 New supports were installed for Boiler Pump 2. BP1 is offsite for repair at the moment.
 Drywall repair in the lobby lower ceiling is being done, with maintenance tiles being 
installed.
 Staff had their photos taken by the Town as part of making photo ID badges for 
Londonderry staff. The goal is to have ID badge-keyfob access in the future.
 Elevator maintenance will take place this week.
 Mold retesting is scheduled for next week; this will be the key determinant in finalizing a 
reopening date. They are rushing this for us.
 Friends of Leach Library will be sharing a booth with Leach staff at Old Home Days.
 Staff have resumed ordering collection materials for FY27, which means patrons will 
have access to new materials soon.
 Over 2,000 items were removed from the collection in June, which includes items that 
are being replaced after flood damage.
 Adult programming: the Awaaba Ensemble was very well-received and Becca has been 
asked to write about it for the NH Humanities Connections Blog!
o There is high demand for adult craft sessions.
o A couple of upcoming programs: What’s Wild in NH, and Adult Graphic Novel 
book discussion
 Summer hours will be in effect until Saturday, 9/12. The satellite location for Leach will 
be closed on Saturday, 8/15 for Old Home Days.
 The CIP presentation will be on Tuesday, 8/18 at 6 PM.
 Chair Hendricks: seeking consideration and consensus from the Board on protocol 
regarding donations from private parties for substantial items. Board consensus is to 
direct those parties to the Chair and the Interim Director.
 Teen/children’s programming: substantial engagement from patrons for programming, 
materials, museum passes, etc. This is great!
o Teens: the movie on the commons and the DIY reading journal were particularly 
popular this month.
o Children’s: Magician Mike is doing a show on 8/11 as a preview for a show at Old
Home Day this year.
 Vice Chair Marrocco: at OHD there will be a quilt raffle at the We Are Londonderry booth
to benefit the Friends.
Treasurer’s Report: presented by Treasurer Palo.
 We don’t have July numbers yet; they will be available at the next meeting.
Committee Reports:
 Bylaws: presented by Secretary Laue. The draft of the bylaws will be made available to 
the full Board and Interim Director Plante for review tomorrow, and presented in the 
special meeting on 8/20.
 Director committee: presented by Treasurer Palo. The job description and posting has 
been amended for clarity and accuracy, and to reflect the hiring process that we wish to 
follow.
Presentations and Discussion:
 FY26 missing financial documentation: presented by Treasurer Palo. Colleen Madgziarz 
and Interim Director Plante have been coordinating with Treasurer Palo to prepare an 
accurate list of financial documentation that is missing, such as deposit slips, voided 
checks, and the checkbook register. Some of these items include a deposit for over 
$30,000.
o “Deposit slips” reflect the procedure followed by Leach staff to document receipts
etc. that are provided by the bank. These are used in audits.
o Citizen’s Bank is only able to provide some materials retroactively; others cannot 
be replaced or recreated.
o TD Bank has not affirmed whether they can provide copies of the deposit slips for
their items.
o We are hoping that this itemized list helps the previous Treasurer find these 
items. Interim Director Plante anticipates being visited by auditors sometime this 
month.
o Interim Director Plante requests a written document on behalf of the Board 
describing the situation and our efforts to retrieve the missing documentation for 
the auditors. Treasurer Palo will draft said document.
 Furniture replacement for second FY26 insurance claim: This is related to the second 
radiator leak that occurred during the initial repair project. The claim covers a round table
that sits directly on the floor, and three end cap displays. Interim Director Plante reports 
that Megan Donovan found end cap displays in storage; she is asking for Board 
consensus regarding the purchasing of a different item with the money, such as two 
wheeled display stands and/or two soft chairs, acknowledging that we would lose the 
depreciation value of the lost items if we do this. We would also be using the recent 
$1,000 furniture donation towards these items.
o Board consensus is to approve research and pricing, to present to the Board at 
the next meeting.
 Tentative reopening process: presented by Interim Director Plante. The date itself is 
based on the mold retesting, but the process would be 1) to request Board approval on 
the date that public operations are closed at the LPD community room and 2) to 
redistribute staff hours to the Monday-Friday prior to the reopening to have all hands on 
deck for moving back in to the building.
o Chair Hendricks requests that we bring in LPD staff for us to give them a public 
thank you for hosting the Library for all these months.
Deliberations and Vote:
 Library director posting: Interim Director Plante has concern that the job description 
leaves a little too much out. She is invited to attend the next subcommittee meeting. 
Motion made by Secretary Laue to delay the vote on this matter until the 
committee has met again, seconded by Trustee Mallick. Motion passes 5-0.
 Purchasing policy and property disposal request form: this is the purchasing policy that 
was presented in July 2026 and was amended by the subcommittee pursuant to Board 
feedback. Motion made by Secretary Laue to accept and adopt the purchasing 
policy and property disposal request form, seconded by Treasurer Palo. Motion 
passes 5-0.
 Funding requests: presented by Interim Director Plante.
o RTU-1 drip pan repair: the drip pan isn’t an ordered item; it is made. The email 
reflects approximately $1,500 in labor charges, but that amount can change 
because labor hours can be unpredictable through the process. The contractor 
also affirms that there is more than the drip pan at stake with RTU-1, and Interim 
Director Plante would like to move forward with a vote regarding all items for 
RTU-1. This would not only allow us to address the long-term issue more 
effectively, but save taxpayers money because every visit from the contractor 
costs an additional fee for transit etc. 
 Chair Hendricks: how do we make a motion when we don’t have a dollar 
amount? Interim Director Plante: use the purchasing policy authorization.
 Motion made by Secretary Laue to approve Interim Director Plante 
using emergency purchasing to cover RTU-1 maintenance and 
repairs, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 5-0.
o Deep cleaning before reopening: $2,400 for “professional construction cleaning,” 
which refers to deep cleaning. As a reminder, we have not been expending our 
full contracted amount for custodial services this FY.
 Motion made by Secretary Laue to expend $2,400 for professional 
construction cleaning out of the custodial services line of the 
budget, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 5-0.
o Stripping and waxing meeting room and lower-level hallway floors: $1,750, to be 
done at the same time as the deep clean. 
 Motion made by Secretary Laue to expend $1,750 for waxing from 
the custodial services line of the budget, seconded by Trustee 
Mallick. Motion passes 5-0.
o Tuition reimbursement additional funding: The current budget covers 1.3 classes 
for each of the two staff members working towards their MLS degrees, and 
leaves no money available for other staff seeking reimbursement. Interim 
Director Plante requests the Board to consider overspending this budget line to 
cover 1.5 ($492) or 2 classes ($2,250) for these staff members. This shortage is 
being addressed as well through the FY28 budget.
 Chair Hendricks: current union negotiations put us in a tricky position to 
respond to this. Vice Chair Marrocco recommends that we seek legal 
counsel to affirm what is and isn’t permissible under status quo.
o Additional flagpole repairs: $893.95 to improve the flag pole operation, but is not 
strictly necessary. Motion by Secretary Laue to expend $893.95 from the 
maintenance line for flagpole repairs, seconded by Treasurer Palo. Motion 
passes 5-0.
o Assabet Interactive room booking module: This adds functionality to the Assabet 
Interactive services we already use. In particular, it allows patrons to reserve 
rooms online through their library card; we could also use this for Talk Box if we 
wanted. This would require staff to undergo a little training and to update the 
Library’s room policy. This was also considered as a CIP project, but has been 
included in the FY28 budget for maintenance. This is $800 annually, with a $150 
one-time setup fee. Motion by Secretary Laue to expend $950 from 
management services to cover this module, seconded by Trustee Mallick. 
Motion passes 5-0.
o Tree trimming/removal: This has been prepared in conjunction with DPW. The 
verbal quote is for $1,600-$1,800 to trim trees that are touching the building roof. 
The trees lining the building’s sidewalk may need to be removed as well, as 
student foot traffic to the high school may necessitate that as snow and ice weigh
branches down.
 Trustee conversation ensues about long-term planning, the community 
value of the trees, balancing that against the safety and well-being of 
pedestrians and staff.
 Motion by Secretary Laue to spend up to $1,800 from maintenance 
for tree trimming, seconded by Trustee Mallick. Motion passes 5-0.
 Contracts:
o Assabet Interactive: Motion by Secretary Laue to expend $1,650 from 
management services for Assabet Interactive, seconded by Trustee Mallick.
Motion passes 5-0.
o A-1 Phoenix janitorial service: Interim Director Plante recommends continuing 
with this service because they do good work and are highly responsive to 
feedback and requests. They are offering a 4% decrease in cost, charging 
$2,195 per month. Motion by Secretary Laue to continue the contract with A-
1 Phoenix for $2,195/month, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. Motion 
passes 5-0.
 Acceptance of Unanticipated Funds under RSA 202-A:4-c and RSA 202-A:4-d:
o $10 anonymous unrestricted donation
o $880 from Friends of the Leach Library to sponsor adult book discussion 
programs, story time program at Sensory Seekers, and Concert on the Common 
for Kids.
o 32 books valued at $508.67 from Friends of the Leach Library. Interim Director 
Plante notes that this kind of donation has been ongoing with the Friends, and 
was particularly beneficial when purchasing was on hold during the transition 
between fiscal years.
 Vice Chair Marrocco notes that any community member can donate $10 
to the Friends to become a Friend.
o Motion made by Secretary Laue to accept these unanticipated funds under 
RSA 202-A:4-c and RSA 202-A:4-d, seconded by Vice Chair Marrocco. 
Motion passes 5-0.
Public Comment:
 Linda Lampkin, 4 Griffin Road: Anyone who wishes to pay $10 to become a Friend of the
Leach Library at Old Home Days will receive a special gift made by Dana.
Adjournment: motion to adjourn made by Secretary Laue at 8:24 PM, seconded by Vice 
Chair Marrocco. Motion passes 5-0.
Minutes prepared by Secretary Laue.
